title: indigo_libs: deliver every update received from a remote server, including unchanged values
description:
Found by the two-server scheduler stress test of ticket ca925388 (indigo_test/integration/run_scheduler_two_servers.py, topology scripting-local).

Symptom: server A (Scheduler + Scripting) connected to server B (Imager Agent + CCD simulator) with -r. A task restarted after ABORT hangs forever in Sequencer.js set_local_mode() at SEQUENCE_STATE step 4: the restart sets the same CCD_LOCAL_MODE values; B sends the setTextVector, but A's bus treats it as a non-update (no item changed, state unchanged, no message) and does not deliver it to the Scripting Agent's client. The same update from a local Imager Agent is delivered, because the local change handler marks items do_update explicitly (indigo_property_copy_values). Setting FORCE_PROPERTY_UPDATES on A's connection to B did not help.

Cause (to confirm): set_property() in indigo_libs/indigo_xml.c updates the cached remote property and calls indigo_update_property(); the change-detection in indigo_update_property() (indigo_bus.c ~1229-1268) compares against previous values and suppresses the update. B already decided to send the update, so the local bus should forward it. Find out why item->do_update set in set_property does not survive (e.g. B sends no items for unchanged values, or flags are cleared), and fix so that a set received from a remote server is always delivered, as for a local device. Check indigo_json.c and the BLOB paths for the same.

Experimental fix that made the test pass: property->do_update = true in set_property() before indigo_update_property() (in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-rumen-work-indigo-git/629be5ae-c7a6-4969-bd2c-27ae612f2bf9/scratchpad/xml_experimental_fixes.patch). Verify it is correct and does not cause update storms or loops in chained servers.

Tests: a protocol-level test of a repeated identical set from a remote server reaching a local client; the two-server test's KNOWN DEFECT markers for this defect must disappear (remove them). Run the existing server/protocol tests.

Replaces sub-ticket 8d835099-43a4-47fc-8ec2-402ea80159d1, so that this fix lands on master as its own commit (owner asked for separate commits). The implementation and tests are the reviewed change of 8d835099-43a4-47fc-8ec2-402ea80159d1, ported unchanged; see that ticket's notes and journal for the reproduction and results.

outcome.summary: Pass. (1) git diff master...HEAD changed lines are byte-identical to ticket/ca925388...ticket/8d835099 (3 files, +62/-2); only offsets differ. (2) Merge coherent: set_property() (indigo_xml.c:553,560) is independent of the new def_property()/update_cached_property(); indigo_define_property clears previous state (indigo_bus.c:1191) so a redefinition followed by a set behaves correctly; test counters are reset by memset in reset_context(), updated_item_count is used only by the new case; all 12 cases registered once, no duplicates. (3) Fix correct: item do_update is now set after the copy (indigo_set_text_item_value clears it for unchanged text, indigo_bus.c:2316-2318), property->do_update forces delivery, including state-only/no-item sets; flags are cleared by clear_previous_state after delivery, so nothing stale carries over; switch reset items and unlisted changes still go through the bus comparison; WO BLOB count=0 and RO BLOB default branch are unaffected. No amplification: one received set gives at most one delivery, and re-sharing remote devices is opt-in (indigo_reshare_remote_devices). Peers that send redundant sets (force_property_updates on their side, legacy INDI) are now forwarded 1:1, as the docs describe. Ran: built libindigo in the worktree, rebuilt test_protocol_xml with LD_LIBRARY_PATH on the worktree build/lib (checked with ldd): 12/12 pass. Negative control (master indigo_xml.c linked over libindigo): new case fails at test_protocol_xml.c:607 (0 of 3 updates); with only the property->do_update line removed, 1 of 3. Note: the two-server test KNOWN DEFECT markers are not on master (run_scheduler_two_servers.py belongs to ca925388), so removing them is left to that ticket.
